grades.quote: The 27-bit VPN is translated into a 44-bit PPN via a three-level page table, while the 12-bit page offset is untranslated.
grades.reason: Describes Sv39 structure (three-level page table, VPN[2:0] fields, PTE format, bits 9-0 same as Sv32). This is background for superpages, but it never says what makes a leaf a superpage or what alignment is needed.
Only a general overview of Sv39 and the rationale for several virtual-memory modes. It says nothing about leaf PTEs, superpages or alignment.
Covers the Svpbmt memory-type bits in PTEs. It doesn't address how a leaf becomes a superpage or the alignment rules.

grades.quote: When all three are zero, the PTE is a pointer to the next level of the page table; otherwise, it is a leaf PTE.
grades.reason: This is the Sv32 section, not Sv39. It gives the R/W/X rule that separates a leaf PTE from a pointer to the next level, which also applies in Sv39. It doesn't mention superpages or alignment.
